content.title: About
content.content: Sausage gravy is a thick sauce made from milk, cream, and browned sausage pieces, seasoned with spices. It is traditionally served over mashed potatoes, eggs, or biscuits. The flavor is rich, creamy, with a subtle smoky note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sausage gravy originated in American cuisine as a quick way to use leftover sausage.
The classic recipe uses a milk base, but variations with broth or cream cheese exist.
It is often served as part of a Southern breakfast alongside fried eggs and toast.
Vegetarian versions replace sausage with soy “links” or mushroom crumble.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The sausage pieces provide animal protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: The dairy base supplies calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Gravy is calorie‑rich, offering a good energy boost in colder months.

items.title: High fat and sodium
items.content: Traditional gravy contains saturated fat and salt, so it should be consumed in moderation, especially by those with cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Milk allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should choose dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Nitrites in sausage
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites, which can be harmful in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the gravy hot, pouring it over mashed potatoes, rice, pasta, or scrambled eggs. Garnish with fresh herbs, black pepper, or hot sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared gravy in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months after cooling and portioning.
